chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from a number of our companions, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about water from which pigeons drink, and he said: Everything whose flesh is eaten—wudu (ablution) may be performed from its leftover water, and it may be drunk.

And about water from which a hawk, falcon, or eagle drinks, he said: From whatever birds drink, wudu (ablution) may be performed, unless you see blood in its beak. If you see blood in its beak, then do not perform wudu (ablution) from it, nor drink from it.

And he was asked about water from which a chicken has drunk, and he said: If there is filth in its beak, then do not drink from it and do not perform wudu (ablution) from it. But if you do not know that there is filth in its beak, then perform wudu (ablution) from it and drink.

And this report is general regarding the permissibility of the leftover water of everything whose flesh is eaten among the rest of the animals, and that whatever flesh is not eaten, the use of its leftover water is not permissible. We have also explained in our book Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām what relates to that, and there we presented the reports fully. What this report includes of the permissibility of the leftover water of birds whose flesh is not eaten, such as the hawk and falcon, when their beaks are free of blood, is specified as an exception from among those whose flesh is not eaten regarding the permissibility of using their leftover water.

key_terms.اسْتِعْمَالُ: the use or application of the leftover water
key_terms.الطُّيُورِ: birds as a legal category in the ruling
key_terms.دَمًا: blood, whose presence renders the water unusable in this context
key_terms.سُؤْرِهِ: the leftover water remaining after an animal or bird has drunk from it
key_terms.قَذَرٌ: filth or impurity present on the beak
key_terms.مِنْقَارِهِ: its beak, examined for visible impurity such as blood
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: whose flesh is lawful to eat
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: one may perform wudu (ablution) with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using the leftover water of birds and animals for wudu (ablution) and drinking?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling on leftover water from which various animals and birds have drunk, especially in relation to wudu (ablution) and drinking. It establishes the permissibility of using the leftover water of animals whose flesh is eaten, while generally disallowing that of animals whose flesh is not eaten, with a specific exception for certain birds when no blood is seen on their beaks.
